precepts.text: A writing sealed with the king's ring may not be reversed, so a second decree is made to deliver the Jews.
precepts.point: He decreed that the cost be paid from the king's tribute beyond the river so the builders would not be hindered. Once a Persian decree was made it was upheld rather than vetoed. Even in Esther a decree against the Jews was not revoked but answered by a stronger decree in their favor.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

precepts.why:
Darius decreed that Tatnai and his companions be far from the work, that the elders of the Jews build the house of God in his place, and that the expenses be paid “of the king’s goods, even of the tribute beyond the river”, so that “they be not hindered.” Once a Persian decree was made it was upheld, not vetoed.

Esther shows the same law. The king tells Esther and Mordecai to “Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring: for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse.” The decree against the Jews could not be revoked, so a second and stronger decree was written in their favor to deliver them.

That is why Darius did not simply cancel what Tatnai had done. Cyrus had made a decree to build the house, and it stood; Darius confirmed it and made his own decree, and once made, no man could reverse it.

precepts.text: The tribe of Levi is given to Aaron and his sons to keep the charge and do the service of the tabernacle.
precepts.point: The priests were set in their divisions and the Levites in their courses as it is written in the book of Moses, every man having his ordered task.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

precepts.why:
At the dedication “they set the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their courses, for the service of God, which is at Jerusalem; as it is written in the book of Moses.” The book of Moses is Numbers 3: “Bring the tribe of Levi near, and present them before Aaron the priest, that they may minister unto him.”

The Levites “shall keep his charge, and the charge of the whole congregation before the tabernacle of the congregation, to do the service of the tabernacle”, and “they shall keep all the instruments of the tabernacle of the congregation, and the charge of the children of Israel.” The Lord gave the Levites to Aaron and his sons: “they are wholly given unto him out of the children of Israel.”

So when the house was finished and the children of the captivity kept the dedication with joy, offering the hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs and twelve he goats for a sin offering for all Israel, it was a great praise, and the Levites' hands were full doing the service. Every man had his ordered task, the priests in their divisions and the Levites in their courses, just as Moses wrote.

points: The elders of the Jews builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo; and they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the God of Israel, and according to the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.

And this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king. Why did the Lord call Haggai and Zechariah? What was their mission? To get on Zerubbabel and Joshua to continue building the temple; they had stopped building because they were being hindered by the other nations. Those two prophets blasted the high priest and the governor so they would go back to the work, and they finished it in the sixth year of Darius.
Darius made search, and in the palace at Achmetha in the province of the Medes the roll was found recording the decree of Cyrus.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: The decree ordered the house rebuilt with strong foundations and set dimensions, the expenses given out of the king's house, and the gold and silver vessels restored to their place. Cyrus helped fund the rebuilding of the house of Israel.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: Darius commanded Tatnai and his companions to leave the work alone and let the elders of the Jews build.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: He decreed that the cost be paid from the king's tribute beyond the river so the builders would not be hindered. Once a Persian decree was made it was upheld rather than vetoed. Even in Esther a decree against the Jews was not revoked but answered by a stronger decree in their favor.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: The king ordered daily provision of bullocks, rams, lambs, wheat, salt, wine, and oil so the priests could offer sacrifices without fail, and that they might pray for the life of the king and his sons.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: Whoever altered the decree was to be hanged on timber pulled from his own house, and his house made a dunghill. The God who caused his name to dwell there was called on to destroy any king or people who tried to destroy this house.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: The elders prospered through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah and finished the house by the commandment of the Most High and of the Persian kings.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: The house was finished, and the children of the captivity kept the dedication with joy, offering a hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve he goats for a sin offering according to the number of the tribes of Israel. This was a great praise, and the Levites' hands were full doing the service.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: The priests were set in their divisions and the Levites in their courses as it is written in the book of Moses, every man having his ordered task.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: The children of the captivity kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, for the priests and Levites were purified together and killed the passover for all the captivity.

note.label: Ezra 6: The Decree Confirmed And The House Dedicated

points: The passover can be kept in captivity with joyfulness and gladness of heart. Going back to the past shows how Israel is meant to operate, and these had the kingdom mindset to see the vision and finish the work.
